continuity_scope: Ridley Scott's original Legend feature production (1985), restricted to the 89-minute U.S. theatrical release cataloged by AFI as released 18 April 1986. AFI documents that Universal shortened/rescored the U.S./Canadian theatrical version from an earlier 93-minute configuration and that the Goldsmith score remained in the international release. This pass uses only the opening prologue and opening-forest plot segment as AFI locates it; it does not combine the international theatrical cut, 2002 Director's Cut, score variants, novelization, deleted material, or later derivative works.
work_or_witnesses: Legend, original Ridley Scott feature, selected U.S. theatrical release (89 minutes; 18 April 1986) of the 1985 production
American Film Institute Catalog record 57395, credits, cut-history note, prologue, and opening-forest synopsis
coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic character in the selected AFI opening prologue/forest segment: Jack, Lili/Lily, the Lord of Darkness, Blix, Honeythorn Gump, Brown Tom, and Nell. Unicorns, goblins, elves, fairies, Darkness as a cosmological condition, light, magic, mortal purity, soul language, the horn, the forest, winter, weapons, and the balance premise are terms/dimensions unless AFI clearly credits or narrates a named acting individual. Performers are not character records. Later named figures and unnamed husband/guards/creatures are excluded because they fall outside the selected opening boundary or lack individual names.
omissions: All named figures first occurring after the selected opening-forest boundary, including Screwball, Pox, Blunder, Oona, and Meg Mucklebones, plus unnamed unicorns, goblins, elves, fairies, trolls, guards, and Nell's unnamed husband.

All exact film dialogue, later scenes, ending/outcome information, specific magical mechanics beyond the selected prologue/segment, actor performance, make-up, voice, stunt, or production-person claims.

The 1985 international theatrical configuration, 2002 Director's Cut, alternate scores, novelization, scripts not authorized for this pass, deleted scenes, home-video bonus material, and derivative/adapted works; fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, reviews, and promotional reproductions.
uncertainties: AFI's catalog is an authoritative film-history source, but its scene synopsis does not give timestamps or a cut-comparison for each listed event. Claims are therefore limited to opening plot material and never claim that a detail is unique to every release version.

The prologue spells the princess Lily, while AFI reports end credits as Lili. Both forms are retained for one person. AFI credits Jack as Jack [o' the Green], Gump as [Honeythorn] Gump, and Darkness as [Lord of] Darkness; bracketed forms are aliases/titles, not separate people.

The prologue calls Lily a girl and the synopsis calls her a princess, but neither supplies an age. No child/youth assertion is made. It establishes affection between Jack and Lili, but does not establish marriage, sexual activity, or consent beyond the limited scene description. The later coercive/captivity material is outside this pass.

The selected segment includes a poisoned unicorn, winter/frozen people, a sword cut to a unicorn horn, and imagined soul danger. These are fictional violence/fantasy elements; no detailed death, injury, self-harm, or real religious/cosmological claim is inferred.
evidence_basis: AFI Catalog record 57395 only: title/release/credit data, AFI's release-history discussion, opening prologue transcription, opening cast credits, and the precise opening-forest synopsis passage. No non-authoritative character database or secondary plot guide is used.
